```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Time to a paying customer: B's hypothesized payer is an individual operator or consultant who can self-fund or expense $49–$299/mo. A's highest-value payers (banks) need 6–18 month sales cycles and SOC 2 Type II before outbound. That is incompatible with a 90-day target.",
    "Hard blockers: A carries biometric-privacy regulatory risk (BIPA's $650M Facebook settlement, Worldcoin investigations in Spain, Thailand and Colombia). B's brief names no comparable compliance gate.",
    "Willingness to pay: B's competitors charge $49–$299/mo, or $60 per blueprint, for near-identical outputs, which shows individuals already pay in this category. A's self-serve tier faces at least two competitors with free entry tiers (useHUMA's free 1,000 verifications/mo; World ID has no public per-call price), pushing the reachable segment's price toward zero.",
    "Enterprise targets: A's brief admits the named enterprise customers are already served, with Zoom on World ID and Incognia on 1B+ devices. That leaves only the crowded self-serve segment.",
    "Acquisition: B's pain is voiced natively on Indie Hackers and LinkedIn, giving a plausible low-cost organic channel to a first customer. This partly offsets the poor paid-ads economics (~$104 CPL against a ~$60 price), though B's organic channels are unquantified.",
    "Buildability: both briefs claim a solo founder can build a working version quickly. That factor does not separate them."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence does not come from anyone who would pay. The marquee quote is from Trevor Traina, Chief Business Officer of Tools for Humanity (World ID), a direct competitor. It is promotional vendor messaging about its own Zoom deal, not buyer demand. The Reddit quote is from a dating-app end user, but the brief itself says the platform, not the end user, is the payer. So no evidence shows a platform willing to pay a new entrant.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. Neither brief has strong demand evidence. B's two quotes show people struggle with decisions, not that they will pay for a dedicated tool over a general-purpose LLM chat. B is also a saturated niche with no identified wedge. B wins mainly because A's path to a first paying customer is blocked by long enterprise sales cycles, compliance requirements, biometric regulatory risk, and free-tier competitors. B's barriers are competitive rather than structural, which matters more under a 90-day constraint."
}
```
